dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether a frozen release still knows which workflow may publish it
dailyInsight.insight: OpenClaw's merged release-tooling change keeps the product's Code SHA/ref separate from the Tooling SHA/ref and, for its covered npm publication route, rechecks an exact protected tag and release-publish parent run immediately before a registry mutation. Builders who maintain release automation should audit whether their own pipeline can distinguish the reviewed workflow revision from a later-moving branch, rather than treating a ref name or old approval as a durable publishing identity.
dailyInsight.mechanism: PR #126881 adds an identity verifier that accepts the protected route only as the exact lightweight `release-publish/<sha>-<run>` tag and matching workflow SHA. It reads the live remote tag reference, rejects a missing, moved, annotated, wrong-SHA, or same-name-branch substitute, and validates the repository, workflow path, head SHA, run ID, run attempt, and allowed state of the release-publish parent run before the covered npm paths proceed.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Release validation and release mutation are separated by time and often by unrelated repository activity. If the workflow identity can silently refresh from a moving branch, a reviewed candidate can reach a privileged writer under different rules. The recommended audit is a dry-run or source-level check of one pipeline boundary; it is not a claim that OpenClaw has shipped a package under this control or that every publisher is covered.

actions.audience: Release engineer or maintainer responsible for a CI path that validates and then publishes a package or artifact
actions.label: Try identity substitution in a non-publishing release rehearsal
actions.instruction: In a disposable repository or a CI dry-run that cannot write a registry, freeze a candidate commit and its workflow revision. Before the final simulated publish step, attempt four substitutions: move or delete the protected tag, replace it with an annotated tag, use a same-name branch, and supply a different approval run or attempt. Confirm from redacted logs that each is rejected and that the normal moving-branch route is not silently used as a fallback.
actions.effort: 30–60 minutes for a dry-run workflow or source-level verifier test

receipts.title: PR #126881: keep protected tooling trusted after main moves
receipts.supports: States the failure when reviewed SHA-pinned release tooling becomes untrusted after main advances, the protected-tag identity model, its immediate publish-boundary verification, and the deliberately narrow npm-only scope.

receipts.title: fix(release): keep protected tooling trusted after main moves (#126881)
receipts.supports: Shows the public merged workflow, release-guide, verifier, and test changes across the release foundation.

receipts.title: Release tooling identity verifier tests at commit fa86caf94
receipts.supports: Shows explicit rejection cases for moved, deleted, annotated, wrong-SHA, and same-name-branch identities, plus separate current-main ancestry handling.

confidence.basis: The fresh public merge, PR scope statement, pinned verifier, release guide, and focused tests agree on one narrow identity-control mechanism. The audit is restricted to a non-publishing rehearsal and does not depend on a claim about release availability.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts are public main-branch source, PR text, documentation, and focused tests. They do not establish that any OpenClaw package has been published under the route, that every privileged writer is protected, that a release has completed successfully after main advanced, or that another CI system has the same behavior.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if a public covered publish path accepts a moved tag, an annotated tag, a same-name branch, or a mismatched parent run; narrow it if the released workflow no longer reads the live protected-tag identity immediately before the npm mutation.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for the dependent writer changes and a public release receipt that carries a frozen tooling identity through the covered npm route after main advances, while still rejecting substituted identities.
